title: secp256k1-ecdlp: truncated-prefix deterministic BSGS at exact 39/100 coverage

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the deterministic truncated-prefix baby-step/giant-step algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^128.321575 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, failures and verification. The covered scalar set is exactly the prefix [0,m^2) with m=212506270031153001307260662621714878127 and 100*m^2 >= 39*r, so the single deterministic attempt succeeds on at least 39/100 of the uniform challenge distribution and the full giant walk is charged even on failure. Peak memory is at most 2^135.320774 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^127.321949 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, retries or heuristic assumptions. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic generic accounting control, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical affine secp256k1 code path (same field modulus, generator, addition formulas, sort key and binary-search lookup) at reduced table size: count field operations per point addition against the C coefficients, check that the sorted baby keys are strictly increasing, recover scalars inside the covered prefix and fail on a scalar just outside it, and re-check the exact full-size coverage and work ledger in integer arithmetic. This does not establish production curve behaviour at full table size, memory bounds, or operation costs by measurement.
